message.text:
Reactions are removed by explicit Go code during user deletion across all three drivers. The reaction table has no foreign key cascade to the user table. Evidence locations are being gathered.

The driver files `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go` and the corresponding SQLite and Postgres equivalents contain `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`. The migration SQL confirms the reaction table has no foreign key cascade. `store/reaction.go` only supports deleting individual reactions by ID, not cascading deletions.

h05.
explicit Go code; store/db/mysql/user_delete.go, store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go, store/db/postgres/user_delete.go; store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql (and mysql/postgres LATEST.sql)

On user delete, each driver runs `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (reactions on the user’s memos) and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (`DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = …`). Example: `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go` around the `deleteUserTargetsTx` calls and those two helpers. The `reaction` table in `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` (same shape in mysql/postgres) has `creator_id` but no `FOREIGN KEY` / `ON DELETE CASCADE` to `user`. `store/reaction.go` only deletes a single reaction by ID.
